title: Navigating the Azure Portal
description: Learn how to navigate the Azure Portal, and get introduced to Azure CLI and PowerShell for managing Azure from the command line.

data.text: The **Azure Portal** (https://portal.azure.com) is a web-based console for managing all your Azure resources. It is the most common way beginners interact with Azure, and it provides a visual, point-and-click interface.

data.title: Key Areas of the Azure Portal
items: **Home** — your personalized dashboard with frequently used resources
**All services** — browse every Azure service by category
**Resource groups** — view and manage all your resource groups
**Cost Management** — track your spending and set budgets
**Help + support** — get assistance and open support tickets

data.text: When you open a resource in the portal, you will see a left-hand menu with options like Overview, Activity Log, Access Control, and Settings. These options change depending on what type of resource you are viewing.
The **Azure CLI** (Command-Line Interface) lets you manage Azure resources from a terminal. It works on Windows, macOS, and Linux. The command prefix is always `az`.

data.title: Common Azure CLI Commands
data.code:
# Log in to your Azure account
az login

# Set your default subscription
az account set --subscription "MySubscription"

# List all resource groups
az group list --output table

# Create a new resource group
az group create --name myResourceGroup --location eastus

# Create a virtual machine
az vm create \
  --resource-group myResourceGroup \
  --name myVM \
  --image UbuntuLTS \
  --admin-username azureuser \
  --generate-ssh-keys

data.text: **Azure PowerShell** is a set of PowerShell modules for managing Azure. It is popular among Windows administrators and users who prefer scripting with PowerShell. The main module is `Az`.

data.title: Common Azure PowerShell Commands
data.code:
# Connect to Azure
Connect-AzAccount

# Set your subscription
Set-AzContext -Subscription "MySubscription"

# List all resource groups
Get-AzResourceGroup

# Create a new resource group
New-AzResourceGroup -Name myResourceGroup -Location EastUS

# Create a virtual machine
New-AzVM -ResourceGroupName myResourceGroup `
  -Name myVM `
  -Image "UbuntuLTS" `
  -AdminUsername azureuser `
  -GenerateSshKey

terms.definition: The web-based console for managing Azure resources visually.
A cross-platform command-line tool for managing Azure resources.
A PowerShell-based command-line tool for managing Azure resources.

items.text: Sign up for an Azure Free Account at azure.microsoft.com/free
Open the Azure Portal at portal.azure.com
Install the Azure CLI and run `az login`
Create your first resource group using the portal or CLI

data.title: Portal vs. CLI vs. PowerShell
data.text: All three tools do the same things — they are just different interfaces. The portal is great for learning, while CLI and PowerShell are better for automation and repeatable tasks. You can use them interchangeably.
